system_type_reason: Monorepo of agents-core plus ~40 provider plugins for building real-time voice/video agents.

repo_overview.summary: Python framework for real-time multimodal voice and video agents. An Agent joins a WebRTC call via an edge transport (Stream by default), processes incoming audio/video through a pipeline (VAD, STT, turn detection, LLM, TTS) or a speech-to-speech realtime LLM, and responds in the call. Tool calling runs inside the LLM plugins as a bounded multi-round loop; the repo is a monorepo of agents-core plus about 40 provider plugins.

components.purpose: Agent class: call lifecycle, event wiring, conversation, agent_launcher (warmup, sessions), inference flows (transcribing vs. realtime), session registry (in-memory/redis), transcript buffer
LLM base class, realtime (speech-to-speech) base, function registry for tool registration and execution
MCP client for local and remote servers, tool conversion
base classes of the speech pipeline
video processors (e.g. YOLO) and avatar audio/video sync
runner and HTTP server that launch agent sessions
audio/video queues, input pacer, forwarders, tokenizer
RAG base, instruction loading, model warmup
test harness with LLM judge and mock tools
CLI: project scaffolding and agent run command
about 40 provider integrations (openai, gemini, anthropic, deepgram, elevenlabs, getstream, ...) holding the concrete LLM tool loops
11 example applications (golf coach, phone + RAG, k8s deployment, ...)

topology.justification: One Agent holds one LLM (agents.py:218) and builds exactly one inference flow around it, either RealtimeInferenceFlow or TranscribingInferenceFlow (agents.py:429-447). STT, TTS, VAD and turn detection are fixed pipeline stages, and tools and MCP servers are callables invoked by that single LLM. Several agents in the same call run as independent sessions with no coordination between them.

resilience.name: session lifetime enforcement (idle timeout and max duration)
resilience.what_it_is: A background maintenance loop in AgentLauncher runs every 5 s (maintenance_interval) and closes sessions whose agent has been alone on the call longer than agent_idle_timeout (default 60 s, 0 disables) or whose call time exceeds max_session_duration_seconds (default None, unlimited).
resilience.function_in_system: Sits outside the per-turn loop at the session-management level of the runner/launcher. Reclaims agents whose users have left and caps the runtime of a single session. Otherwise orphaned agents keep the call connection, STT/LLM/TTS streams and provider billing alive indefinitely.

resilience.name: session admission limits
resilience.what_it_is: start_session rejects new sessions with MaxConcurrentSessionsExceeded / MaxSessionsPerCallExceeded once max_concurrent_sessions (node-wide) or max_sessions_per_call (checked against the shared session registry) is reached. Both default to None (unlimited).
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the entry point where the runner spawns a new agent for a call. Bounds the number of simultaneously running agents per node and per call. Otherwise a burst of join requests overloads the node and multiplies provider costs, and several agents can end up talking in the same call.

resilience.name: session liveness via TTL heartbeat in the shared registry
resilience.what_it_is: Every session record in the session registry store (in-memory by default, Redis for multi-node) expires after a TTL of 30 s. The launcher's maintenance loop rewrites each record of its own sessions every 5 s via update_metrics (only_if_exists). Close requests from any node are stored as TTL flags in the same registry; the owning node polls them in each maintenance cycle and closes the flagged sessions.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the session-management level shared by all runner nodes, outside the per-turn loop. Records of a crashed or stalled node expire on their own, so the per-call session limit and cross-node lookups only count live sessions, and a client can stop an agent through any node (e.g. a beacon request when the browser tab closes). Otherwise ghost sessions of a dead node block new agents for that call permanently, and agents whose client went away keep running until the idle timeout.

resilience.name: barge-in interruption of the agent turn
resilience.what_it_is: When turn detection signals that a participant started speaking (TurnStarted), or a realtime LLM reports interrupted audio output, interrupt() cancels the in-flight LLM turn, calls llm.interrupt(), flushes pending transcripts, clears LLM output and TTS input/output queues and stops TTS playback.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the inference flow between user input and agent output (TranscribingInferenceFlow and RealtimeInferenceFlow). Aborts the current response as soon as the user takes the floor, so the next turn is based on the new utterance. Otherwise the agent keeps speaking an outdated answer over the user and spends LLM/TTS tokens on output nobody hears.

resilience.name: speculative (eager) LLM turns with cancel on transcript change
resilience.what_it_is: On an eager end-of-turn signal the LLM call starts before the turn is confirmed; its output is buffered in the LLMTurn and only streamed to TTS after confirm()/finalize(). If the transcript changes in the meantime, the running turn is cancelled (task cancel plus llm.interrupt()) and a new turn starts with the updated transcript.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in TranscribingInferenceFlow between turn detection/STT and the LLM call. Hides LLM latency behind the confirmation window and discards responses to stale transcripts. Otherwise the agent either waits for full confirmation before querying the LLM (higher response latency) or speaks answers to an incomplete utterance.

resilience.name: drop-when-busy for injected prompts
resilience.what_it_is: simple_response(text, interrupt=False) checks under a lock whether an LLM turn is in flight (started, unfinalized, uncancelled) and silently drops the injected prompt in that case. The default interrupt=True preempts the running turn instead.

Per the docstring it avoids cascade cancellations from periodic callers. Otherwise every periodic trigger cancels the current answer, and the agent never completes a response while burning LLM calls.

resilience.name: component warmup with shared resource cache
resilience.what_it_is: Components with expensive resources (VAD models, YOLO processors, local STT/TTS, turn detection) implement Warmable. A launcher-wide WarmupCache keyed by component class loads each resource once via on_warmup() under a per-class lock and hands the cached resource to every new agent via on_warmed_up(). The launcher runs a dry-run warmup at startup.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in session setup, before an agent joins a call. Saves model loading time and memory per session, since parallel sessions share one loaded resource. Otherwise every new session reloads or redownloads its models, which raises join latency and memory use per session.

resilience.name: bounded tool-calling rounds per turn
resilience.what_it_is: The multi-hop loop (LLM response, tool execution, tool results back to the LLM) stops after max_tool_rounds / tools_max_rounds rounds, default 3, and the last response is emitted. The same default of 3 is set in all 12 tool-capable LLM plugins (openai, chat_completions, anthropic, gemini, aws, xai, openrouter, minimax, inworld, huggingface).
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside LLM.simple_response of each plugin, i.e. inside one agent turn. Caps the number of LLM calls and tool executions a single user utterance can trigger. Otherwise a model that keeps requesting tools runs an unbounded chain of calls, which stalls the spoken reply and multiplies token cost.

resilience.name: tool-call deduplication within a turn
resilience.what_it_is: Tool calls are keyed by id/name/serialized arguments; a seen-set carried across all rounds of a turn skips any call whose key was already executed. Prevents repeated execution of identical tool calls that the model re-emits in a later round or the stream delivers twice. Otherwise side-effecting tools run multiple times and each repeat adds latency and cost.

resilience.name: MCP call retry with auto-reconnect
resilience.what_it_is: All MCP operations (list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource, list_prompts, get_prompt) go through _call_with_retry: up to 3 attempts, each attempt first ensures a connection (reconnecting if needed), and after a failure the client disconnects and waits 1 s before the next attempt. After the last attempt the error is re-raised.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the MCP client base class under every MCP tool call the agent makes. Absorbs dropped connections and restarts of local or remote MCP servers. Otherwise a single transport hiccup makes the tool call fail and removes the MCP tools from the conversation until a manual reconnect.

resilience.name: MCP idle session timeout
resilience.what_it_is: A background monitor checks every 10 s the time since the last MCP activity and disconnects the session after session_timeout (default 300 s) without tool traffic. The next MCP call reconnects through _ensure_connected.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the MCP client base class alongside the agent's session. Releases idle MCP connections and local server subprocesses during long calls that use no tools. Otherwise idle connections and subprocesses stay open for the whole session, and stale remote sessions fail on the next tool call.

resilience.name: automatic reconnect of provider streaming connections with backoff
resilience.what_it_is: STT, TTS and realtime plugins re-establish their websocket/stream to the provider after transient failures, each implemented per plugin: AWS Transcribe with unlimited attempts and backoff min(2^n, 30 s) driven by a reconnect event; AssemblyAI with 3 attempts and backoff 0.5 s doubling to 4 s; ElevenLabs STT with 3 attempts and 2^n s backoff; Qwen realtime reconnecting after a fixed backoff only for transient websocket close codes 1011-1014; Inworld TTS reconnecting on a dropped websocket.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the provider plugins that feed the agent's speech pipeline (audio in via STT, audio out via TTS, speech-to-speech via realtime LLMs). Keeps the long-lived streaming connection of a live call alive across network drops and provider restarts. Otherwise a single connection loss leaves the agent deaf or mute for the rest of the call.

resilience.name: error classification with session resumption in the Gemini Live loop
resilience.what_it_is: Exceptions in the Gemini Live processing loop are classified into reconnect (websocket/API codes 1011-1014), stop (clean close or other codes) or retry (anything else). Reconnect re-establishes the session passing the last session_resumption handle stored from server updates; retries stop after 5 consecutive errors and the realtime session is marked disconnected.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the receive loop of the Gemini realtime (speech-to-speech) LLM. Separates transient provider faults from terminal ones and resumes the same server-side conversation after a reconnect. Otherwise transient faults end the conversation or lose the dialogue state, and persistent faults spin in an endless error loop.

def _classify_loop_error(exc: Exception) -> tuple[str, str, bool]:
    """Classify a processing-loop exception into (action, reason, clean)."""

        case websockets.ConnectionClosedError(rcvd=rcvd):

resilience.name: HTTP retry with exponential backoff for xAI TTS
resilience.what_it_is: The xAI TTS request is retried up to 3 times on HTTP 429/500/503 and on aiohttp client errors, waiting 2^n s between attempts, with a 60 s total timeout per request; other status codes raise immediately.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the TTS plugin at the end of the pipeline, where the agent's text reply is turned into speech. Absorbs rate limits and transient server errors of the TTS provider. Otherwise a rate-limit spike drops the spoken answer of that turn.

evidence.snippet:
max_retries = 3
for attempt in range(max_retries):
    try:
        async with session.post(
            self._base_url,
            json=payload,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=60),
        ) as resp:
            ...
            if resp.status in (429, 500, 503):
                wait = 2**attempt
                ...
                await asyncio.sleep(wait)
                continue
    ...
    except aiohttp.ClientError as e:
        if attempt < max_retries - 1:
            wait = 2**attempt
            logger.warning("Network error: %s, retrying in %ds", e, wait)
            await asyncio.sleep(wait)
            continue
        raise

raise RuntimeError("xAI TTS: max retries exceeded")

resilience.name: frame-rate throttling and rolling frame buffer for vision LLMs
resilience.what_it_is: Video frames reach the model at a reduced rate: VideoForwarder calls each frame handler at most at its configured fps; the VLM plugins (Gemini, OpenAI chat completions) default to fps=1 into a deque with maxlen fps * frame_buffer_seconds (default 10 s, i.e. 10 frames) and send only these buffered frames per request; the OpenAI realtime video track also defaults to 1 fps.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the incoming WebRTC video track (up to 30 fps) and the multimodal LLM input. Bounds the number of images per LLM request and per second of call. Otherwise every turn pushes a full-rate video stream into the model, which multiplies image tokens, cost and latency and overflows the context window.

evidence.snippet:
fps: int = 1,
frame_buffer_seconds: int = 10,
...
self._frame_buffer: deque[av.VideoFrame] = deque(
    maxlen=fps * frame_buffer_seconds
)
...
"""Convert buffered video frames to JPEG bytes."""
frames = list(self._frame_buffer)
